<!--
  TRACK HOME PAGE — one block per profile, chosen by Quarto itself (when-profile).

  This page deliberately contains NO R code. It used to build its content in an R chunk from
  Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROFILE"), but `freeze: auto` keeps ONE cached result per file for all
  profiles, so every track ended up showing whichever track was rendered last (Basic opened the
  GIS home page). Plain markdown is never frozen, so each profile always gets its own block.

  Every block has the same order:  banner → game → self-study plan → goals → downloads → tip.
  Link only to files that exist in the repository: Quarto copies linked files into the track site.
-->

::: {.callout-warning}
This page was rendered without a track profile. Render with `quarto render --profile basic` (or another profile), or run `bash render-all-profiles.sh`.
:::

[Basic Track]{.ws-track-title}

Step 1 of the self-study path. Start here if you are new to R: you will set up R, wrangle a dataset, draw your first plots, choose a statistical test and write a reproducible report.
:::

::: {.ws-track-game}
🗺️ **Play as you learn.** This track is **Region 1 · Basics** of *Dungeons & Dataframes*. Take the pre-test, read a step below, then clear the matching world.
[Open the game →](../dungeons/dungeons/index.html){.ws-track-game-btn}
:::

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

Work through the steps in order. Every page ends with a **self-check quiz**, and each step has a **lab** (an R script with blanks to fill in; it reads the [NCD survey](data/ncd_survey.csv)). Keep the [Basic cheat sheet](cheatsheets/basic.qmd) open. Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Set up R and write your first lines**

    [Getting Started](r-foundations/getting-started.qmd): install R and RStudio, objects, vectors and data frames. Lab: [b1_first_script.R](labs/basic/b1_first_script.R).

2.  **Wrangle a dataset**

    [Data Wrangling (Tidyverse)](r-foundations/data-wrangling.qmd), then [Merging Datasets](r-foundations/merging_dataset.qmd). Practise with the [Practice Slides](r-foundations/data_wrangling_prac_s.qmd). Labs: [b2_tidy_data.R](labs/basic/b2_tidy_data.R) · [b3_joining.R](labs/basic/b3_joining.R).

3.  **Draw your first plots**

    [Grammar of Graphics](data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd), then copy and adapt examples from the [Basic Plot Gallery](plot-gallery/basic.qmd). Lab: [b4_first_plots.R](labs/basic/b4_first_plots.R).

4.  **Choose and run a statistical test**

    [Test Selection Guide](statistical-analysis/statistical_tests.qmd), then [ggstatsplot — Intro](ggstatsplot/ggstatsplot_intro.qmd) to plot a test and its result together. Lab: [b5_which_test.R](labs/basic/b5_which_test.R).

5.  **Meet regression**

    [Regression Analysis](statistical-analysis/regression.qmd): a first look. The Regression track covers it in depth.

6.  **Write it up**

    [Quarto Basics](quarto_repro_w/reproducible_writing.qmd): turn your code and results into a report. Lab: [b6_first_report.R](labs/basic/b6_first_report.R).

7.  **Check yourself and move on**

    Take the Region 1 post-test in the game. At 70% or more, continue with the **Moderate** track (Step 2 on the main page).
:::

## 🎯 What you will be able to do

- Use R to import, clean and reshape data
- Build clear basic plots with ggplot2
- Pick a suitable statistical test and read its output
- Produce a reproducible report with Quarto

## 📥 Downloads

- Track cheat sheet: [Basic track cheat sheet](cheatsheets/basic.qmd)
- Labs: [b1](labs/basic/b1_first_script.R) · [b2](labs/basic/b2_tidy_data.R) · [b3](labs/basic/b3_joining.R) · [b4](labs/basic/b4_first_plots.R) · [b5](labs/basic/b5_which_test.R) · [b6](labs/basic/b6_first_report.R); data: [ncd_survey.csv](data/ncd_survey.csv) · [ncd_round1.csv](data/ncd_round1.csv) · [ncd_round2.csv](data/ncd_round2.csv) · [villages.csv](data/villages.csv)
- Posit cheat sheets: [RStudio IDE](downloads/cheatsheets/rstudio-ide.pdf) · [Data import](downloads/cheatsheets/data-import.pdf) · [Data transformation](downloads/cheatsheets/data-transformation.pdf) · [Data visualization](downloads/cheatsheets/data-visualization.pdf) · [R Markdown](downloads/cheatsheets/rmarkdown.pdf)
- Example scripts: [Intro](downloads/source-scripts/nctoh/Intro.R) · [Data wrangling](downloads/source-scripts/nctoh/data_wrangle.R) · [Data visualization](downloads/source-scripts/nctoh/data_vis.R)
- Everything else is on the [Downloads](downloads.qmd) page.

> 💡 **Tip:** New to R? Do not skip Step 1. Everything later assumes it.

:::

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

Work through the steps in order. Every page ends with a **self-check quiz**, and each step has a **lab** (an R script with blanks to fill in). Keep the [Moderate cheat sheet](cheatsheets/moderate.qmd) open. Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Refresh the basics** (skip if you finished the Basic track)

    [Getting Started](r-foundations/getting-started.qmd) · [Data Wrangling (Tidyverse)](r-foundations/data-wrangling.qmd) · [Merging Datasets](r-foundations/merging_dataset.qmd)

2.  **Clean messy data and stop repeating yourself**

    [Cleaning Messy Data](r-foundations/cleaning_messy_data.qmd), then [Iteration (across, loops, functions)](r-foundations/iteration.qmd). Labs: [m1_cleaning.R](labs/moderate/m1_cleaning.R) · [m2_iteration.R](labs/moderate/m2_iteration.R).

3.  **Learn what makes a plot good**

    [Grammar of Graphics](data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd) · [Best Practices](data-visualization/best_practices.qmd) · [Matching Data to Plots](data-visualization/plot_data.qmd)

4.  **ggplot2 in depth**

    [Module 1 — Foundations & Geoms](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_1_foundations_geoms.qmd), then [Module 2 — Aesthetics, Faceting & Themes](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_2_aesthetics_faceting_themes.qmd).

5.  **Widen your plot vocabulary**

    [Basic](plot-gallery/basic.qmd) and [Intermediate](plot-gallery/moderate.qmd) plot galleries, then [Merged Visuals](specialized/merge_visuals.qmd) and [Statistical Plots](specialized/plot_stats.qmd). Lab for steps 3–5: [m3_explore_plots.R](labs/moderate/m3_explore_plots.R).

6.  **Tests and tables for a paper**

    [Test Selection Guide](statistical-analysis/statistical_tests.qmd) · [ggstatsplot — Intro](ggstatsplot/ggstatsplot_intro.qmd) · [ggstatsplot — Intermediate](ggstatsplot/ggstatsplot_moderate.qmd) · [gtsummary Tables](gtsummary/gtsummary_tutorial.qmd) · [Data Analysis](statistical-analysis/data_analysis.qmd) · [Regression Analysis](statistical-analysis/regression.qmd). Labs: [m4_table1.R](labs/moderate/m4_table1.R) · [m5_tests.R](labs/moderate/m5_tests.R).

7.  **Reports that update themselves**

    [Quarto Basics](quarto_repro_w/reproducible_writing.qmd), then [Quarto — Dynamic Documents](quarto_repro_w/quarto_moderate.qmd).

8.  **Export your figures**

    [Exporting Plots](exporting_tools/exporting_plots.qmd) · [Plotting Tools](exporting_tools/plotting_tools.qmd). Lab for steps 7–8: [m6_report.R](labs/moderate/m6_report.R).

9.  **Check yourself and move on**

    Take the Region 2 post-test in the game, then continue with the **Regression** track (Step 3 on the main page).
:::

## 🎯 What you will be able to do

- Clean real, messy data and automate repeated steps
- Apply design principles and ggplot2 modules 1–2 to your own figures
- Build a Table 1 and other summary tables with gtsummary
- Write Quarto documents whose numbers update with the data

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

One session a day is a comfortable pace: read the slides, answer the quiz on the last slides, then do the lab. Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Check your R basics**

    [Getting Started](r-foundations/getting-started.qmd) · [Data Wrangling (Tidyverse)](r-foundations/data-wrangling.qmd)

2.  **See the whole map first**

    [Regression Analysis](statistical-analysis/regression.qmd): simple, multiple, logistic and Cox regression and diagnostics on one page.

3.  **Session 1 — Foundations**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s1_foundations.qmd) · [Lab 1](regression-workshop/labs/lab1_explore.R)

4.  **Session 2 — Simple Linear Regression**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s2_simple_regression.qmd) · [Lab 2](regression-workshop/labs/lab2_simple.R)

5.  **Session 3 — Inference & Multiple Regression**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s3_multiple_regression.qmd) · [Lab 3](regression-workshop/labs/lab3_multiple.R)

6.  **Session 4 — Assumptions**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s4_assumptions.qmd) · [Lab 4](regression-workshop/labs/lab4_assumptions.R)

7.  **Session 5 — Logistic Regression**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s5_logistic_regression.qmd) · [Lab 5](regression-workshop/labs/lab5_logistic.R)

8.  **Session 6 — Interpreting & Reporting**

    [Slides and quiz](regression-workshop/s6_reporting.qmd) · [Lab 6](regression-workshop/labs/lab6_reporting.R)

9.  **Keep the cheat sheet, then move on**

    [Interpretation Cheat Sheet](regression-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd). Take the Region 3 post-test in the game, then continue with the **Advanced** track (Step 4 on the main page).
:::

## 🎯 What you will be able to do

- Fit and interpret simple and multiple linear regression models
- Screen predictors and build a multivariable model
- Fit logistic and Cox models for binary and time-to-event outcomes
- Check assumptions with base R and the `performance` package
- Report a model for a thesis or a paper

## 📥 Downloads

- Dataset: [Simulated NCD survey (CSV)](data/ncd_survey.csv), n = 600 in 20 villages · [make_data.R](regression-workshop/make_data.R) rebuilds it
- Labs (fill in the `___` blanks): [Lab 1](regression-workshop/labs/lab1_explore.R) · [Lab 2](regression-workshop/labs/lab2_simple.R) · [Lab 3](regression-workshop/labs/lab3_multiple.R) · [Lab 4](regression-workshop/labs/lab4_assumptions.R) · [Lab 5](regression-workshop/labs/lab5_logistic.R) · [Lab 6](regression-workshop/labs/lab6_reporting.R)
- Cheat sheets: [Data import](downloads/cheatsheets/data-import.pdf) · [Data transformation](downloads/cheatsheets/data-transformation.pdf)
- Everything else is on the [Downloads](downloads.qmd) page.

> 💡 **Tip:** Do the lab on the same day as its session. The labs reuse one dataset, so each one starts where the last one ended.

:::

[Advanced Track]{.ws-track-title}

Step 4 of the self-study path. The complete visualization library (all four ggplot2 modules, advanced and interactive plots, publication-ready Quarto) and nine advanced analysis workshops, A1 to A9. Each workshop has five slide decks with a quiz, five R labs and a two-page cheat sheet.
:::

🗺️ **Play as you learn.** Region 4 · Advanced of *Dungeons & Dataframes* is not built yet. Regions 1 to 3 are a quick way to check the foundations this track assumes.
[Open the game →](../dungeons/dungeons/index.html){.ws-track-game-btn}
:::

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

Steps 1 and 2 finish the visualization library. Steps 3 to 11 are the workshops: do A1 to A3 first, then take the others in the order your own work needs. Every session is listed on [Advanced Workshops](advanced-workshops.qmd). Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Finish ggplot2 and the plot galleries**

    [Module 3 — Colors, Scales & Themes](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_3_colors_scales_themes.qmd) · [Module 4 — Advanced Best Practices](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_4_advanced_best_practices.qmd) · [Advanced Plot Gallery](plot-gallery/advanced.qmd) · [Practical Applications](plot-gallery/practical_application.qmd) · [Interactive Plots](specialized/interactive.qmd)

2.  **Publication-ready output**

    [ggstatsplot — Advanced](ggstatsplot/ggstatsplot_advanced.qmd) · [Quarto — Publication](quarto_repro_w/quarto_advanced.qmd) · [Debugging Plots](exporting_tools/debugging_plots.qmd) · [Advanced Exporting](exporting_tools/advanced_exporting.qmd)

3.  **A1 · Survival analysis**

    Time-to-event data, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox. [Start at Session 1](survival-workshop/s1_time_to_event.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](survival-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

4.  **A2 · Counts and rates**

    Poisson and negative binomial regression, offsets, excess zeros. [Start at Session 1](counts-workshop/s1_counts_rates.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](counts-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

5.  **A3 · Ordinal and multinomial outcomes**

    Ordinal logistic regression, the proportional-odds check, multinomial models. [Start at Session 1](ordinal-workshop/s1_categorical_outcomes.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](ordinal-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

6.  **A4 · Clustered and repeated data**

    ICC, cluster-robust standard errors, GEE, mixed models. [Start at Session 1](clustered-workshop/s1_clustered_data.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](clustered-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

7.  **A5 · Survey data and weights**

    Complex survey design, weights, `svyglm`, raking. [Start at Session 1](survey-workshop/s1_survey_design.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](survey-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

8.  **A6 · Curves and interactions**

    Splines, GAMs, effect modification, prediction plots. [Start at Session 1](curves-workshop/s1_beyond_linear.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](curves-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

9.  **A7 · Missing data**

    MCAR, MAR and MNAR, multiple imputation with `mice`, sensitivity analysis. [Start at Session 1](missing-workshop/s1_patterns_mechanisms.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](missing-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

10. **A8 · Prediction models**

    Risk models, discrimination and calibration, validation, shrinkage, decision curves. [Start at Session 1](prediction-workshop/s1_building_model.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](prediction-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)

11. **A9 · Causal inference**

    DAGs, adjustment, propensity scores, inverse probability weighting, E-values. [Start at Session 1](causal-workshop/s1_causal_questions_dags.qmd) · [Cheat sheet](causal-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd)
:::

## 🎯 What you will be able to do

- Use all four ggplot2 modules and build advanced and interactive figures
- Produce publication-ready documents with Quarto
- Choose and fit the right model for survival, count, ordinal, clustered and survey data
- Handle non-linear effects, interactions and missing data properly
- Build and validate a prediction model, and reason about causal questions

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

Work through the steps in order. Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Understand how a plot is built**

    [Grammar of Graphics](data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd)

2.  **Learn what makes a plot good**

    [Best Practices](data-visualization/best_practices.qmd), then [Matching Data to Plots](data-visualization/plot_data.qmd).

3.  **ggplot2 Module 1**

    [Foundations & Geoms](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_1_foundations_geoms.qmd)

4.  **ggplot2 Module 2**

    [Aesthetics, Faceting & Themes](data-visualization/gram_ggplot/module_2_aesthetics_faceting_themes.qmd)

5.  **Build your plot vocabulary**

    [Basic Plots](plot-gallery/basic.qmd), then [Intermediate Plots](plot-gallery/moderate.qmd).

[GIS and Spatial Statistics Track]{.ws-track-title}

An elective track. A five-session workshop on spatial data and spatial statistics in R: maps with `sf`, neighbours and weights, Moran's I, local clusters and hot spots, and spatial regression. All examples use a synthetic district of 80 blocks with a planted hot spot, so no real boundaries or personal data are involved. The full visualization library is in the navbar as well.
:::

::: {.ws-track-game}
🗺️ **Play as you learn.** A GIS region of *Dungeons & Dataframes* is not built yet. Regions 1 to 3 cover the R, plotting and regression this track assumes.
[Open the game →](../dungeons/dungeons/index.html){.ws-track-game-btn}
:::

## 🗓️ Self-study plan

Each session pairs a slide deck (with a quiz on the last slides), a longer reading page and a lab. Tick a step when you have finished it; ticks are saved in this browser.

::: {.ws-plan}
1.  **Check the prerequisites**

    [Getting Started](r-foundations/getting-started.qmd) · [Data Wrangling (Tidyverse)](r-foundations/data-wrangling.qmd) · [Grammar of Graphics](data-visualization/ggplot_grammar.qmd). Session 5 also assumes linear regression.

2.  **Session 1 — Spatial data and maps**

    [Slides and quiz](gis-workshop/s1_spatial_data.qmd) · read [Spatial Data with sf](gis/spatial_data_sf.qmd) and [Maps and Choropleths](gis/maps_choropleth.qmd) · [Lab 1](gis-workshop/labs/lab1_data.R)

3.  **Session 2 — Neighbours and spatial weights**

    [Slides and quiz](gis-workshop/s2_neighbours_weights.qmd) · read [Neighbours and Spatial Weights](gis/spatial_weights.qmd) · [Lab 2](gis-workshop/labs/lab2_weights.R)

4.  **Session 3 — Global spatial autocorrelation**

    [Slides and quiz](gis-workshop/s3_global_autocorrelation.qmd) · read [Global Moran's I](gis/morans_i.qmd) · [Lab 3](gis-workshop/labs/lab3_global.R)

5.  **Session 4 — Local clusters and hot spots**

    [Slides and quiz](gis-workshop/s4_local_clusters.qmd) · read [Local Moran's I (LISA)](gis/local_moran_lisa.qmd) and [Geary's C, Getis-Ord, Join Counts, Scan Statistic](gis/other_spatial_tests.qmd) · [Lab 4](gis-workshop/labs/lab4_local.R)

6.  **Session 5 — Spatial regression and reporting**

    [Slides and quiz](gis-workshop/s5_spatial_regression.qmd) · read [Spatial Regression and Residual Tests](gis/spatial_regression.qmd) · [Lab 5](gis-workshop/labs/lab5_regression.R)

7.  **Keep the cheat sheet**

    [Spatial Statistics Cheat Sheet](gis-workshop/cheatsheet.qmd): a two-page guide to choosing and reading spatial tests.
:::

## 🎯 What you will be able to do

- Read, transform and join spatial data with `sf`, and keep track of coordinate reference systems
- Make clear static and interactive maps and choose a sensible classification
- Define neighbours and spatial weights, and know how the choice changes the answer
- Test for global spatial autocorrelation with Moran's I and read the Moran scatterplot
- Locate clusters and outliers with local Moran's I (LISA) and hot spots with Getis-Ord Gi\*
- Check regression residuals for spatial structure

## 📥 Downloads

- Data: [district_blocks.geojson](data/gis/district_blocks.geojson) · [facilities.csv](data/gis/facilities.csv) · [make_gis_data.R](gis/make_gis_data.R) rebuilds them
- Labs (fill in the `___` blanks): [Lab 1](gis-workshop/labs/lab1_data.R) · [Lab 2](gis-workshop/labs/lab2_weights.R) · [Lab 3](gis-workshop/labs/lab3_global.R) · [Lab 4](gis-workshop/labs/lab4_local.R) · [Lab 5](gis-workshop/labs/lab5_regression.R)
- General cheat sheets are on the [Downloads](downloads.qmd) page.

> 💡 **Tip:** Never mapped data in R? Spend extra time on Session 1 before moving on. Everything later depends on getting the spatial object and its coordinate system right.

:::

```{=html}
<script>
// Self-study plan: a tick box on every step, remembered in this browser (per track).
(function () {
  var hero = document.querySelector('.ws-track-hero[data-track]');
  var steps = document.querySelectorAll('.ws-plan > ol > li');
  if (!hero || !steps.length) return;
  var key = 'ws-plan:' + hero.getAttribute('data-track');
  var done = {};
  try { done = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) || '{}') || {}; } catch (e) { done = {}; }
  // the landing page's profile card reads these totals
  try { localStorage.setItem('ws-plan-total:' + hero.getAttribute('data-track'), String(steps.length)); } catch (e) {}

  var status = document.createElement('p');
  status.className = 'ws-plan-status';
  var plan = document.querySelector('.ws-plan');
  plan.parentNode.insertBefore(status, plan);

  function refresh() {
    var n = 0;
    steps.forEach(function (li, i) {
      var on = !!done[i];
      li.classList.toggle('ws-plan-done', on);
      li.querySelector('.ws-plan-tick').checked = on;
      if (on) n++;
    });
    status.textContent = n + ' of ' + steps.length + ' steps done';
  }

  steps.forEach(function (li, i) {
    var box = document.createElement('input');
    box.type = 'checkbox';
    box.className = 'ws-plan-tick';
    box.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Mark step ' + (i + 1) + ' as done');
    box.addEventListener('change', function () {
      if (box.checked) done[i] = 1; else delete done[i];
      try { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(done)); } catch (e) {}
      refresh();
    });
    li.appendChild(box);
  });
  refresh();
})();
</script>
```
